unit.title: Marketing automation and deliverability
unit.description: Drip and trigger emails, lifecycle, preference center, list hygiene, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI, IP warming, sender reputation

cards.definition: The first automated emails after a sign-up. They get the best open rates of all emails: deliver what was promised, set expectations, then guide toward a first action.
cards.example: Day 0: the guide. Day 2: the best article. Day 5: a case study. Day 8: a demo offer.

cards.term: Gmail and Yahoo bulk sender rules
cards.definition: Since 2024, senders of more than 5,000 emails a day to Gmail or Yahoo must authenticate with SPF, DKIM and DMARC, offer one-click unsubscribe and keep spam complaints below 0.3 percent.
cards.example: A newsletter without DMARC starts landing in spam at Gmail.

cards.definition: A short sequence sent to inactive subscribers to win them back or let them go. Those who do not react are removed, which protects deliverability.
cards.example: Still interested? Click here to keep receiving our tips, or we will stop writing to you.

exercises.prompt: A visitor leaves a cart and receives an email two hours later. What kind of email is it?
choices: A behavioural trigger email
A newsletter
A drip campaign by date
A transactional receipt
exercises.explain: Trigger emails react to an action (or a missing one). They usually convert far better than scheduled broadcasts.

exercises.prompt: Which DNS record lists the servers allowed to send email for your domain?
choices: SPF
DKIM
DMARC
BIMI
exercises.explain: SPF lists authorized senders. DKIM signs each message, DMARC says what to do when checks fail, BIMI shows your logo.

exercises.prompt: Which record tells mailbox providers what to do when SPF and DKIM fail, and sends you reports?
choices: DMARC
SPF
DKIM
MX
exercises.explain: DMARC policies go from none (monitor) to quarantine and reject. Start with none, read the reports, then tighten.

exercises.prompt: You move to a new dedicated IP for your emails. What do you do?
choices: Warm it up: raise volumes gradually over a few weeks
Send to the whole list on day one
Send only to inactive subscribers first
Turn off authentication during the move
exercises.explain: A new IP has no reputation. Start with your most engaged contacts and grow volumes step by step.

exercises.prompt: Since 2024, bulk senders to Gmail must offer one-click unsubscribe and keep spam complaints under 0.3 percent.
exercises.explain: True. Gmail and Yahoo also require SPF, DKIM and DMARC. Above the threshold, emails go to spam or get rejected.

exercises.prompt: Why remove subscribers who have not opened anything for a year?
choices: They hurt sender reputation and inflate costs
The law requires deleting them after 6 months
They always mark every email as spam
They make the newsletter load slower
exercises.explain: Inactive addresses lower engagement signals, can turn into spam traps and cost money on volume-based tools.

exercises.prompt: What is a preference center for?
choices: Letting subscribers choose topics and frequency
Storing the passwords of your subscribers
Ranking subscribers by their purchases
Hiding the unsubscribe link from users
exercises.explain: Giving a choice (weekly digest instead of daily, only promotions) turns unsubscribes into downgrades.

exercises.prompt: Which email of a welcome sequence usually gets the highest open rate?
choices: The first one, sent right after sign-up
The fifth one, sent after two weeks
A promotional email after one month
They all get the same open rate
exercises.explain: Interest peaks at sign-up. Send the promised content at once, then build the habit.

choices: Asking one or two new questions at each form
Asking every question on the very first form
Buying extra data about leads from brokers
Guessing the job of a lead from their email
exercises.explain: Short forms convert better. Known fields are hidden and replaced by new questions on the next visit.

exercises.prompt: Put a basic lifecycle in order for a subscription app.
steps: Activation nudges until the first key action
Regular value emails to build the habit
Upsell when usage shows a need
exercises.explain: Lifecycle marketing sends the right message at each stage instead of the same newsletter to everyone.
